audit.title: VRF Billing

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens with a serviceable scope statement and each section leads with a quotable claim ("The premium is charged as a percentage of the overall gas cost"). Weak point: content is buried inside `TabsContent` (Subscription / Direct funding) — the canonical answer to "what determines VRF cost" is split across tab panels rather than a single liftable lead.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean H1→H4 hierarchy, 0 level skips, 7 tables, sections all under 600 words — good chunk boundaries. The nested tab components risk interleaving Subscription and Direct-funding facts when an engine chunks the raw markdown.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Strong — 500 gwei gas lane, 100000 callback gas limit, 20% vs 24% premiums, 0.15/0.18/0.186 ETH worked results. Best dimension on the page.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 15 links but only 2 external and **0 to primary sources**. The `fallbackWeiPerUnitLink` and `fulfillmentFlatFeeLinkPPMTier1` parameters are named but never linked to the coordinator contract source or spec.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Crisp verbatim-liftable definitions exist ("Gas lane: The maximum gas price you are willing to pay for a request in wei"). Good.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: No JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. Head could not be verified — but all measured signals are absent.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: 0 fenced code blocks detected; formulas are rendered as plain/untagged blocks. Acceptable for a billing page, but formula blocks are not language-tagged and there is no copy-pasteable estimation snippet.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers setup→estimate→premium→examples for both funding methods, but no troubleshooting/FAQ and no symptom phrasing. The revert condition ("If the consuming contract doesn't have enough funds, your request will revert") is buried in prose, not a findable heading.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Unambiguous, terminology consistent (VRF v2.5, LINK, native token). Only one vague quantifier ("quickly"). Strong.

audit.summary: This is a well-structured VRF 2.5 billing page with strong quantitative content — worked cost examples in both ETH and LINK, explicit gas parameters, and premium formulas (64 numerals, 7 tables). Its biggest GEO weaknesses are missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical, no dates) and two apparently truncated example sections ("Estimate VRF request cost" and "Direct funding cost examples") that promise calculations they never show. The single biggest opportunity is adding symptom/query-phrased headings ("How much does a VRF request cost?", "Why did my VRF request revert?") — the page contains the facts but does not surface them under the questions developers actually type.

recommendations.title: Complete the truncated example sections
recommendations.where: `#### Estimate VRF request cost` and `### Direct funding cost examples`
recommendations.issue: "These example calculations show a cost breakdown…" — then no calculation follows.
recommendations.change: Add the actual worked tables (gas price × components, premium applied, ETH→LINK conversion) mirroring the minimum-balance examples above. An empty promise section is worse than none for retrieval.
recommendations.why: Engines lift complete worked examples verbatim; a section that names a calculation but omits it produces truncated or hallucinated answers.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased headings and a short FAQ
recommendations.where: new H2 near the end, and reword existing H3s.
recommendations.issue: No heading matches "how much does VRF cost" or "why did my request revert".
recommendations.change: Add questions like "How much does a VRF 2.5 request cost?", "Why did my VRF request revert / fail with insufficient funds?", "What happens if I underestimate the callback gas limit?" — answer each in the first sentence, reusing existing body text.
recommendations.why: Developers and agents query by symptom; concept-titled prose loses retrieval the page would otherwise win.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and dateModified
recommendations.issue: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no dates.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified`, canonical `https://docs.chain.link/vrf/v2-5/billing`, and `inLanguage`. (Confirm the CLI passed raw `<head>`; if it didn't, verify before assuming absence.)
recommendations.why: Freshness and structured metadata raise agent trust and parseability (E-E-A-T).

recommendations.title: Lead each section with a method-agnostic canonical statement before the tabs
recommendations.issue: The core cost formula is only visible after selecting a tab panel.
recommendations.change: Precede `TabsContent` with one liftable sentence, e.g. "VRF 2.5 request cost = (gas price × (verification/overhead gas + callback gas)) × (1 + premium%), plus a flat coordinator fee for direct funding." Then let tabs specialize.
recommendations.why: A self-contained lead survives chunking and prevents engines from merging Subscription and Direct-funding facts.

recommendations.title: Link named parameters to primary sources
recommendations.change: Link these to the VRF coordinator/wrapper contract source (GitHub or Etherscan) rather than only the internal Supported Networks page.
recommendations.why: Inline links to primary sources raise citation rate and let agents verify parameter names.

recommendations.title: Language-tag the formula blocks
recommendations.change: Fence formulas with a consistent tag (e.g. ` ```text `) so parsers treat them as extractable code, and consider one copy-pasteable estimation snippet.
recommendations.why: Tagged blocks chunk cleanly and are more reliably reproduced.

recommendations.title: Replace the vague quantifier
recommendations.where: "when Chainlink VRF bumps the gas price to fulfill your request quickly."
recommendations.change: Replace with the actual mechanism/target if known, or drop the adverb.

antiPatterns: Two sections announce example calculations but contain none ("Estimate VRF request cost", "Direct funding cost examples") — unresolved promise / truncated content.
Content locked inside `TabsContent` components risks interleaving Subscription vs Direct-funding facts during RAG chunking.
No stale-date issue detectable (no dates present at all — separate metadata gap).
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal; verify it lists this URL.
JSON-LD/canonical/date emission is template-level; fixing it benefits the whole `docs.chain.link/vrf` tree, not just this page.
The CLI did not capture `<head>`; pass raw head HTML on the next run to confirm the metadata gaps before treating them as final.
